commitResults.messageBody:
# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/Deadline.java
#	src/main/java/Event.java
#	src/main/java/Jason.java
#	src/main/java/Task.java

Move console input, welcome/goodbye messages, errors, and task feedback out of Main and Input into a dedicated Ui class. Keep Input's legacy constructor and preserve the existing user-visible behavior while establishing the first separation of responsibilities for the Jason refactoring.

Move task-file loading, saving, serialization, date-time parsing, and persistence error handling from Jason into a dedicated Storage class. Let Jason coordinate task mutations while Storage owns the file format and TaskList accept loaded tasks during construction. Preserve the existing save path and command-line behavior.

Move command-type detection, task-index parsing, and todo/deadline/event construction out of Input and into a dedicated Parser class. Keep Input focused on executing parsed commands and delegating user-facing output to Ui, while preserving existing command behavior and compatibility.

Make Jason the application coordinator by moving the UI lifecycle, command-reading loop, and error recovery into a public run method. Reduce Main to the minimal entry point that constructs Jason and starts it, completing the current separation among Ui, Storage, Parser, TaskList, and the application controller.

Replace Input's command execution path with an abstract Command and concrete add, list, mark, unmark, delete, and exit commands. Make Parser return executable commands, have Jason run the target-style parse/execute loop, and show divider lines around each interaction. Update the UI test plan for the intentional console output change.

Make Parser dispatch directly to concrete Command implementations, replacing the now-unneeded CommandType intermediary. Delete Input and CommandType after confirming no source references remain, completing the command-hierarchy cleanup without changing the user-facing behavior.

Keep src/main/java as the source root while grouping application classes under jason, commands under jason.command, task models under jason.task, persistence under jason.storage, UI under jason.ui, and custom exceptions under jason.exception. Update imports and the UI test plan to launch the packaged jason.Main entry point.

commitResults.messageBody:
Add assertions for task loading, command parsing, task serialization,
and save-record parsing.

These assertions document assumptions that should always hold and help
reveal programming errors during development without replacing normal
input or file-error handling.

Reduce Parser.parseTask to a task-type dispatch method and move each
validation and construction path into a focused helper.

This keeps the parser method below the guideline's long-method threshold,
keeps each helper at one level of abstraction, and preserves the existing
command formats and validation exceptions.

Reduce Storage.fromSaveFormat to record validation, type dispatch, and
completion-state restoration. Move todo, deadline, and event record
construction into dedicated helper methods.

This keeps the loader easier to read, separates record-specific parsing
logic, and preserves malformed-record handling and the existing save-file
format.

Replace repeated string concatenation in TaskList.toString with a
StringBuilder that appends each formatted task and the final count.

This avoids repeatedly creating intermediate strings as the list grows
and makes the method's output-building steps clearer without changing
the displayed task-list format.

Extract parsing, command tracking, and command execution into one private
method used by both Jason.run and Jason.getResponse.

This removes duplicated orchestration logic, keeps command behavior
consistent between the text UI and GUI response path, and makes each
caller responsible only for its user-interface-specific handling.

Parse index commands using trimmed, whitespace-delimited tokens so
commands with repeated spaces are handled consistently with other parser
paths. Add unit and UI test cases for this input form.

This removes an avoidable input-format inconsistency without changing
normal command behavior or existing validation errors.

Trim command input and split on arbitrary whitespace in Parser.parse and
Parser.parseTask, matching the behavior already provided by parseIndex.
Add unit and UI coverage for commands with leading and repeated spaces.

This removes inconsistent command handling while preserving existing
command formats and validation errors.

Replace repeated task-type and completion-status literals in Storage with
named constants used by both serialization and loading.

This makes the save-file format self-documenting, reduces the risk of
inconsistent literals, and preserves the existing storage representation.

Replace repeated command keyword literals in Parser with named constants
shared by top-level command dispatch and task parsing.

This makes the supported command vocabulary explicit, reduces duplication,
and lowers the risk of inconsistent command strings while preserving
existing parser behavior.

Replace inline user-facing strings in Ui with descriptive constants for
dividers, task results, search results, and count messages.

This centralizes presentation text, makes message ownership explicit, and
reduces the chance of inconsistent wording when responses are updated.

Transfer the welcome, help, and goodbye message constants from Jason to
Ui, which owns displaying all user-facing text. Update the GUI to use
the UI-owned help message.

This improves separation of responsibilities while preserving the exact
CLI and GUI messages.

Define the exit command word in ExitCommand and reuse it in Parser and
MainWindow instead of duplicating the literal value.

This gives the exit command a single source of truth, prevents future
parser-GUI drift, and preserves existing command behavior.

Add a shared CommandWords utility containing the supported command
keywords and update Parser, ExitCommand, and MainWindow to use it.

This gives command recognition a single source of truth, prevents drift
between the CLI and GUI, and preserves existing command behavior.

Use an indexed IntStream and joining collector to build the numbered
task-list output instead of concatenating strings in a loop.

This applies the Java Streams feature to the collection transformation,
avoids repeated intermediate strings, and preserves the existing output
format.
Document internal invariants with Java assertions

Extend todo commands with an optional /for duration modifier. Store

durations as validated java.time.Duration values and persist them as

total minutes in a fourth todo record field while preserving existing

three-field todo records.

Add canonical hour-and-minute display, validation from one minute through

24 hours, user-facing format guidance, storage round-trip coverage, and

CLI test-plan documentation. Keep duration todos as ordinary todos so

existing list, search, completion, and deletion behavior remains unchanged.
